t: You're at Willoughby House, a mid-rise terrace block on the Barbican Estate. It's named after Catherine Willoughby, Baroness Willoughby de Eresby, who lived at the courts of Henry the Eighth, Edward the Sixth, Mary the First and Elizabeth the First. She was the fourth wife of the Duke of Suffolk, and she was a close friend of Henry's last queen, Catherine Parr. The house also has a link to Mary Frith, born here in 1584, who became known as Moll Cutpurse, a notorious pickpocket and fence in London's underworld.
